name: call_library_vector_42
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 42 from that base, discarding any result. Nothing else happens in the routine.

name: forward_single_argument
description: Passes its one 32-bit argument unchanged to another routine and returns nothing of its own. It adds no checks or other work.

name: allocate_block_from_free_list
description: Walks a linked list of free blocks and carves out a block of the requested size, rounded up to whole longwords, splitting off the leftover space when it is large enough. When no free block fits, it falls back to other routines to obtain more memory and returns that result.

name: call_with_error_status
description: Clears a status flag, optionally runs a routine first when a pending flag is set, then calls another routine with its three arguments. If that call returns minus one, it stores the status from another routine and sets an error code of 5 before returning the result.

name: call_library_vector_48
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 48 from that base, discarding any result. Nothing else happens in the routine.

name: call_then_check_status
description: Calls a routine with the first argument and returns minus one if that yields zero. Otherwise it calls another routine with all three arguments and returns minus one when the status flag is set, or the result when it is clear.

name: allocate_linked_memory_block
description: Requests a block 12 bytes larger than the caller's size, stores that total size in the block header, and links the block onto a global list. It returns the address just past the 12-byte header, or zero when the allocation fails.

name: map_zero_to_minus_one
description: Forwards its argument to another routine and passes a nonzero result straight back. A zero result is converted to minus one instead.

name: return_constant_minus_one
description: Returns the value minus one with no other work, serving as a fixed return value for its caller. The pseudo-code has no other behaviour.

name: process_and_clear_node_list
description: Walks a global linked list node by node, passing each node and its third longword to another routine. Afterwards it resets the list head and the associated count to zero.

name: append_node_to_list
description: Appends a node to the tail of a doubly linked list whose header holds the head and tail pointers, setting the node's forward link to empty and its back link to the old tail. If the list was empty, the new node also becomes the head.

name: call_library_vector_210
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 210 from that base, discarding any result. Nothing else happens in the routine.

name: call_library_vector_198
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 198 from that base, discarding any result. Nothing else happens in the routine.

name: combine_result_by_mode
description: Calls another routine with a value picked from a global table by the mode argument, and records error code 22 when that call fails. Mode 2 returns the result of a zero-argument call, mode 1 adds the second argument to the call result, mode 0 returns the second argument, and any other mode returns the mode value itself.

name: call_library_vector_66
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 66 from that base, discarding any result. Nothing else happens in the routine.

name: find_table_entry_by_key
description: Searches an array of eight-byte entries, up to a global count, for one whose first word is nonzero and whose key field matches the argument, and returns its address. If no entry matches it records error code 9 and returns zero.

name: multiply_32bit_words
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values taken from the data registers using 16-bit partial products, adding the two cross terms to the low-word product. The result is the 32-bit product.

name: divide_signed_32bit_values
description: Divides two signed 32-bit values, routing negative operands through other routines and negating the result when needed. A divisor whose high word is zero takes a shorter 16-bit path, while other divisors are normalized before a 16-bit estimate is corrected.

name: normalize_fixed_point_divide
description: Divides a 32-bit dividend by a 32-bit divisor after shifting both to normalize the divisor, returning the quotient in the high longword and the remainder in the low longword of a 64-bit result. A divisor with a zero high word takes a separate direct path.

name: call_with_repeated_second_argument
description: Passes its two arguments to another routine, repeating the second argument as the third, and returns nothing.

name: free_block_into_list
description: Returns a block of the given size to an address-sorted free list, merging it with an adjacent free block before or after it when they touch. It returns minus one for a non-positive size or when the block overlaps a free block, and zero otherwise.

name: read_masked_input_bits
description: Calls another routine with a mask of 12288 and returns the masked bits when any are set. If a hook is installed, it runs the hook first and returns zero when the hook reports failure, otherwise it also calls another routine with 20 before returning the bits.

name: forward_call_without_arguments
description: Calls another routine with no arguments and returns nothing. It adds no other work.

name: call_library_vector_306
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 306 from that base, discarding any result. Nothing else happens in the routine.

name: call_library_from_struct_base
description: Reads a library base pointer from the field 20 bytes into the structure passed in, then calls the library function at offset minus 30 from that base. Nothing is returned.

name: setup_pointer_chain
description: Initialises a small list header in the block it is given: the first longword points 4 bytes past the block start, the second longword is cleared, and the third longword points back to the block.

name: allocate_and_register_record
description: Obtains an identifier, then allocates a record and fills its fields from the two arguments and the identifier. It registers the record through one of two routines depending on whether the first argument is zero; if the record allocation fails, it releases the identifier and returns zero.

name: teardown_registered_record
description: Tears down a record created earlier: if its pointer field is set it first calls a routine on the record, then marks its status byte as 255 and sets a longword to minus one. It finishes by calling two routines with the stored identifier byte and the value 34.

name: call_with_fixed_code_48
description: Passes its argument to another routine together with the fixed value 48 and returns nothing.

name: allocate_typed_record
description: When the first argument is nonzero, allocates a record of the size given by the second argument, then stores a type byte of 5, the second argument as a short, and the first argument in it. It returns the record address, or zero when the first argument is zero or the allocation fails.

name: call_library_vector_294
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 294 from that base, discarding any result. Nothing else happens in the routine.

name: call_library_vector_30
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 30 from that base, discarding the result.

name: call_library_vector_198
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 198 from that base, discarding the result.

name: call_library_vector_210
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 210 from that base, discarding the result.

name: call_library_vector_222
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 222 from that base, discarding the result.

name: call_library_vector_360
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 360 from that base, discarding the result.

name: install_code_hooks_and_jump
description: Stores its incoming base pointer, calls two routines through offsets 52 and 40 from that base, and conditionally writes a fixed byte value. It then writes jump-to-routine instructions into several code locations and finishes by transferring control through a stored pointer.

name: patch_code_and_tables
description: Writes a long sequence of fixed constants and jump-to-routine instructions into a table of code locations, including a run of identical word stores and several 16-bit patches. It calls eighteen other routines along the way and ends by calling through a table entry.

name: store_constants_then_dispatch
description: Writes eight fixed constants to a global location in sequence, then calls two other routines and makes an indirect call through a table pointer.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Stores the value 2 in a global location. The code after that is bad instruction data, so the routine is a stub that does nothing more.

name: write_constants_and_dispatch
description: Writes a fixed sequence of constants to a global location, with several calls to other routines in between. It finishes with an indirect call through a table pointer.

name: write_constants_and_dispatch
description: Writes a fixed sequence of constants to a global location, with several calls to other routines in between. It finishes with an indirect call through a table pointer.

name: write_constants_and_dispatch
description: Writes a fixed sequence of constants to a global location, with several calls to other routines in between. It finishes with an indirect call through a table pointer.

name: write_constants_and_dispatch
description: Writes a longer fixed sequence of constants to a global location, with more calls to other routines in between. It finishes with an indirect call through a table pointer.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without touching any register or memory. The body is empty.

name: replace_words_matching_pattern
description: Scans 16-bit words from a start address up to an end address. Wherever a word equals the first value and the word before it lies between 11071 and 15697 excluding three reserved codes, the word is overwritten with the replacement value.

name: replace_matching_word_pair
description: Scans 16-bit words up to an end address. Wherever a word equals the first value and the word after it equals the second value, the second word is replaced with the third value.

name: clear_high_byte_of_operands
description: Scans 16-bit words up to an end address. Where a word matches one of three fixed codes, the word two positions later is compared against several reference values and, if it matches one, its high byte is cleared so only the low byte remains.

name: replace_word_three_after_match
description: Scans 16-bit words up to an end address. Wherever a word equals the first value and the word three positions later equals the second value, that later word is replaced with the third value.

name: replace_word_two_after_match
description: Scans 16-bit words up to an end address. Wherever a word equals the first value and the word after it equals the second value, the word two positions later is replaced with the third value.

name: shift_stack_longwords_down
description: Copies a longword from the pointer argument into a global location, then shifts a block of thirteen longwords on the stack down by one longword. The calls it makes to other routines are not shown in the pseudo-code.

name: patch_matching_code_sequences
description: Walks a code region in two-byte steps and, wherever it finds one of two fixed instruction sequences, overwrites it with a jump or call instruction that points to another routine.

name: read_longword_field_masked
description: Reads a longword from offset 4 of its pointer argument, calls a routine through a table entry, and returns that longword masked to its low 20 bits.

name: call_check_and_callback
description: Calls another routine, then calls a function from a table at offset 36 of its pointer argument. When that returns nonzero it calls the table entry at offset 8; the referenced text is Password, but the code shows only these calls.

name: dispatch_by_global_flag
description: When a global flag is zero, calls the table entry at offset 36 of the pointer argument and, if that returns nonzero, calls the entry at offset 8. Otherwise it calls the table entry at offset 12 twice.

name: call_table_entry_twice
description: Calls another routine, then calls the table entry at offset 12 of its pointer argument twice, and returns the first argument unchanged.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately with no work; the body is empty.

name: install_jump_hooks_then_start
description: Writes jump-to-routine and call-to-routine instruction words at two fixed code locations, then transfers control to the start routine.

name: wait_for_blitter_idle
description: Calls the blitter-wait routine and then makes a store to a global location that writes its own value back. The store has no effect.

name: start_blit_and_wait
description: Writes a fixed value to the blitter size register, which starts a blit, then loops until bit 6 of that register reads as clear.

name: set_blitter_mask_after_wait
description: Waits for the blitter to finish, then writes a longword with ones in its high word and zeros in its low word to a field 68 bytes into its base structure.

name: set_blitter_word_after_wait
description: Waits for the blitter to finish, then stores the word the wait routine left in the data register at offset 66 from its base structure.

name: call_table_entry_260
description: Calls a routine through a table entry 260 bytes from a base pointer held in a data register, then returns.

name: spin_in_infinite_loop
description: Does no other work and loops forever without returning. The facts list the background colour and raster position registers as touched, but the shown pseudo-code does not write them.

name: copy_block_then_jump
description: Clears a global location, copies a block of code pointer entries from the routine's own area to a second location, then calls into the copied block.

name: call_single_unnamed_routine
description: Makes one call to another routine. Its pseudo-code is unavailable because the decompiler timed out, so the only evidence is that single call and its six-instruction length.

name: configure_hardware_then_loop
description: Calls another routine and then loops forever. The hardware it touches includes the interrupt and DMA control registers, the copper list pointer, and the fire-button and disk status port.

name: install_default_interrupt_vectors
description: Writes the mask 32767, with the top bit clear, to the interrupt and DMA control registers to disable them, clears the first longword, and fills the low vector table with the address of a shared stub that returns from exceptions. The fill covers a long run of entries.

name: write_interrupt_request_value
description: Writes the value 7 to the interrupt request register.

name: relocate_loaded_hunks
description: Walks a list of AmigaDOS hunk records, copying code and data hunks into their destination buffers and adding base offsets to longwords for each relocation record. It returns when the hunk list ends.

name: relocate_loaded_hunks
description: Walks a list of AmigaDOS hunk records, copying code and data hunks into their buffers and adding base offsets for relocation records. It returns when it meets an unknown hunk type or the list ends.

name: relocate_loaded_hunks
description: Copies hunk data and applies relocation records for a sequence of AmigaDOS hunks. It returns when the hunk type codes stop matching the known code, data and relocation values.

name: decompress_backwards_stream
description: Unpacks a compressed block by reading its bit stream backwards and writing decoded bytes from the end of the output area toward its start. Each step either emits literal bytes or copies a run from earlier output, using a table of length codes.

name: decompress_backwards_stream
description: Unpacks a compressed block by reading its bit stream backwards and writing decoded bytes from the end of the output area toward its start. Each step either emits literal bytes or copies a run from earlier output, using a table of length codes.

name: continue_backwards_decompression
description: Continues the backwards bit-stream decoding by handling literal runs and back-references and writing output downward. It returns once the output position reaches its bound and calls one other routine along the way.

name: copy_distance_classed_runs
description: Decodes further backwards-stream output for the decompressor, copying runs from earlier output in three distance classes that use bit widths of 9, 5 and 14, and emitting literals in between. It stops at the output bound and calls one other routine.

name: copy_distance_classed_runs
description: Continues the backwards decompressor by copying runs from earlier output in distance classes, writing literal output downward. It calls one other routine and returns once the output bound is reached.

name: start_disk_read_operation
description: Configures the disk controller for a read: it writes the fixed sync word 17545 to the disk sync register, enables disk DMA and interrupt bits, and sets drive select bits through the CIA port. It then calls two other routines to carry out the transfer.

name: control_disk_drive_lines
description: Writes a sequence of bit patterns to a CIA port to select a drive and set its control lines, with a counter that decrements on each pass. It calls two other routines during the sequence.

name: pulse_disk_drive_step_lines
description: Drives the disk drive control port through a sequence of clear and set writes, separated by calls to other routines, and waits on a status bit before finishing. It makes three calls to other routines along the way.

name: decode_mfm_sector_data
description: Selects a drive through a CIA port and decodes encoded disk data by recombining odd and even bit fields of each longword pair. It calls five other routines along the way.

name: set_disk_dma_length
description: Computes a transfer length from its argument, stores it with a sector count in the disk length register, sets drive control bits through a CIA port, and calls two other routines to prepare the transfer.

name: read_disk_words_into_buffer
description: Sets drive control bits through a CIA port, then copies 16-bit words from the disk data register into a buffer while calling three other routines. Counters decide how many words are read.

name: decode_mfm_buffer_pairs
description: Decodes buffered pairs of encoded longwords by combining their odd and even bit fields, and sets a control bit on the CIA port. It calls one other routine.

name: poll_disk_controller_bounded
description: Runs a loop bounded at 1000 iterations over the disk data register, writing two fixed values to the disk controller and setting CIA control bits. It calls two other routines during the loop.

name: decode_mfm_track_sectors
description: Decodes a track of encoded data by recombining odd and even bit fields from a buffer and placing each decoded block at an offset scaled by 1032 bytes. It also reads and writes disk controller state and calls four other routines.

name: process_disk_track_data
description: A large block of disk-handling code of 259 instructions that the decompiler only partly recovers. The visible pseudo-code loads a value through an address register and makes one call, so its full behaviour is not established from this evidence.

name: advance_disk_buffer_position
description: Adjusts a global offset by a fixed amount and restores it around two calls to other routines, while advancing a read position in the disk buffer.

name: disable_disk_dma_interrupts
description: Writes disable masks to the interrupt and DMA control registers and adjusts a global offset around three calls to other routines.

name: reset_disk_controller_state
description: Writes fixed values to the disk control and interrupt mask registers, clearing a global flag first when it is set and then writing further mask values. It calls one other routine.

name: set_drive_select_bits
description: Writes a drive select bit pattern to a CIA port, adjusts a counter around two calls to other routines, and then clears the same port bits.

name: call_single_unnamed_routine
description: Pseudo-code is unavailable because the decompiler timed out. The evidence is 12 instructions and a single call to another routine.

name: wait_disk_ready_then_read
description: Waits for a status bit in the disk port to be set, toggles drive control bits through the CIA port, stores a buffer pointer in the device block, and reads from the disk data register. It calls four other routines along the way.

name: enter_disk_read_block
description: A two-instruction entry point that makes one call to another routine. The following code runs into disk-read logic that the decompiler does not separate cleanly.

name: reset_disk_status_bytes
description: Clears the high bit of one status byte and zeroes three other status bytes at fixed offsets from a base pointer, then loops until a 16-bit value built from two of those bytes meets its condition.

name: save_and_disable_interrupts
description: Writes the mask 32767 to the interrupt enable register to disable all interrupts, saves the interrupt enable register value into a global, and then writes the mask 32239 with bit 15 clear to clear the listed DMA bits.

name: restore_saved_interrupts_and_dma
description: When its saved flag is set, clears the flag, disables the DMA and interrupt bits, restores saved register values and sets their enable bit. It waits for a raster line and calls two other routines.

name: build_copper_display_list
description: Builds a copper list in memory by writing display control and pointer values, then sets the copper list location from a computed address. It waits for a raster line and calls one other routine.

name: build_copper_display_list
description: Builds an alternate copper list with different display control values, using the same waiting and pointer steps as the other copper list builder. It calls one other routine.

name: configure_copper_and_interrupts
description: Pseudo-code is unavailable because the decompiler timed out. The listed facts show it touches the copper list pointer and jump registers, interrupt and DMA control, and the fire-button and disk status port, and it calls one jump-table entry and four other routines.

name: install_default_interrupt_vectors
description: Writes the mask 32767 to the interrupt and DMA control registers to disable them, clears the first longword, and fills the low vector table with a shared routine address.

name: install_default_interrupt_vectors
description: Repeats the interrupt-disable and vector-table fill steps, then calls seven other routines. It touches the DMA and interrupt control registers along the way.

name: return_without_action
description: A single-instruction routine with no visible work, so it returns immediately.

name: write_interrupt_request_value
description: Writes the value 7 to the interrupt request register.

name: write_cia_interrupt_control
description: Writes the value 8 to a CIA interrupt control location and also touches the interrupt request register.

name: write_interrupt_request_value
description: Writes the value 112 to the interrupt request register.

name: write_interrupt_request_value
description: Writes the value 1920 to the interrupt request register.

name: write_interrupt_request_value
description: Writes the value 6144 to the interrupt request register.

name: write_interrupt_request_value
description: Writes the value 8192 to the interrupt request register and also touches the second CIA interrupt control location.

name: relocate_loaded_hunks
description: Walks hunk records, copying hunk data and adding relocation offsets for each relocation record. It follows the same pattern as the other hunk loader routines in this file.

name: decompress_backwards_stream
description: Starts a backwards bit-stream decompression pass by reading the stream position and a table of codes, then dispatches to the decoding steps. It calls one other routine.

name: emit_literal_bytes_backwards
description: Copies literal bytes from the bit stream into the output, writing downward from the end of the buffer. It calls two other routines and uses a fixed count offset of 108.

name: copy_single_or_double_run
description: Decodes a one-bit length code from the backwards bit stream and copies a run of one or two bytes from earlier output. It calls one other routine.

name: copy_short_run_from_stream
description: Decodes a two-bit length code and copies a run of three to six bytes from earlier output. It calls one other routine.

name: copy_medium_run_from_stream
description: Decodes a four-bit length code and copies a run of seven to 22 bytes from earlier output. It calls one other routine.

name: copy_long_run_from_stream
description: Decodes an eight-bit length code and copies a run of 23 to 278 bytes from earlier output. It calls two other routines.

name: copy_distance_classed_runs
description: Copies runs from earlier output using a fourteen-bit distance class, with branches for several run length classes. It calls two other routines.

name: copy_nine_bit_distance_run
description: Copies a run from earlier output using a nine-bit distance field, writing downward into the output. It calls two other routines.

name: copy_five_bit_distance_run
description: Copies a run from earlier output using a five-bit distance field, writing downward into the output. It calls two other routines.

name: copy_fourteen_bit_distance_run
description: Copies a run from earlier output using a fourteen-bit distance field, with the source offset built from the bit stream. It calls one other routine.

name: initialise_audio_playback
description: Sets up the sound playback state from a data block, initialises counters, and calls one other routine. It also touches the four audio volume registers, the interrupt enable register and the CIA ports.

name: silence_audio_channels
description: Sets the volume of all four audio channels to zero, writes a fixed value to the audio control state, and clears one bit of a global flag.

name: scale_channel_volumes
description: Scales a sample volume by per-channel factors using a multiply and a shift by six, then stores the results in the channel records and sets their counters.

name: install_audio_callback
description: Stores a routine address in a callback field of a structure, sets a counter to 25, clears a count, and points the audio channel 0 location register at a buffer. It calls two other routines.

name: update_channel_period
description: Subtracts a per-step value from a channel counter, resets it to 113 when needed, and looks up a period value from a global table indexed by a nibble of the channel state. It calls two other routines.

name: advance_channel_pointer
description: Advances a channel pointer by a fixed offset, decrements a counter, and busy-waits while a status word is zero before updating the channel period. It calls one other routine.

name: update_channel_playback_state
description: Copies pointer and length fields between channel state records and sets the CIA timer control register. It calls three other routines.

name: lookup_channel_frame_word
description: Stores a byte from the stream into a channel record, then uses a masked byte as a table index and stores the looked-up word in the record. It calls one other routine.

name: lookup_channel_frame_word
description: Uses a masked byte from the stream as a table index and, when that byte is nonzero, loads a word from the table into the channel record. It calls one other routine.

name: set_channel_note_fields
description: Stores a byte from the stream into two channel fields, one of them decremented by one, and looks up a table word from a masked index. It calls one other routine.

name: reset_audio_timer_state
description: Copies a global value, writes 8192 to a global standing in for the interrupt request register, and sets a counter to 25. It touches the second CIA control and interrupt control registers and the DMA control register.

name: reset_audio_interrupt_state
description: Writes 8192 to a global standing in for the interrupt request register and touches the audio channel 0 location register and the second CIA interrupt control register.

name: setup_display_and_copper
description: Disables interrupts, sets the copper list pointer and display control registers, and loads values from data before calling several other routines, including one at a fixed address.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Only two instructions decode here, and the store sequence that follows does not match a real routine, so this is bad instruction data overlapping the start of the next routine rather than usable behaviour.

name: setup_blitter_and_sprites
description: Sets up blitter registers for masks, modulo, pointers, control and size, then sets the pointers for four sprite channels and two colour registers. It calls several other routines.

name: build_sprite_control_words
description: Fills 128 four-word blocks of hardware sprite control data, taking each horizontal position modulo 320 and offsetting it by 128 while two words come from a coordinate table. The routine is one of several entry points into this loop.

name: build_sprite_control_words
description: Fills 128 four-word blocks of hardware sprite control data, taking each horizontal position modulo 320 and offsetting it by 128 while two words come from a coordinate table. The routine is one of several entry points into this loop.

name: build_sprite_control_words

name: build_sprite_control_words
description: Fills 128 four-word blocks of hardware sprite control data, taking each horizontal position modulo 320 and offsetting it by 128 while two words come from a coordinate table. The routine is one of several entry points into this loop.

name: build_sprite_control_words
description: Fills 128 four-word blocks of hardware sprite control data, taking each horizontal position modulo 320 and offsetting it by 128 while two words come from a coordinate table. The routine is one of several entry points into this loop.

name: build_sprite_control_words
description: Continues the sprite control builder, filling further blocks with horizontal positions taken modulo 320 and offset by 128.

name: configure_blitter_registers
description: Configures blitter registers for the first-word mask, control and destination modulo, and writes the interrupt enable register. The pseudo-code is empty, so the exact values are not visible.

name: advance_table_index_counter
description: Increments a global counter twice, subtracts 1535 from another counter, computes a table address from a stored index, and sets a loop count of 127.

name: advance_table_index_counter
description: Updates the global counters in the same way as its neighbour, computes a table address from a stored value, and runs a 127-step loop that calls one other routine.

name: build_offset_lookup_table
description: Fills a table of 1024 entries with running offsets, each one advanced by twice a value read from a second table. It writes into a fixed memory region.

name: call_four_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls another routine four times in sequence and returns. It adds no other work.

name: mix_global_with_constants
description: XORs a global value with several fixed words, rotates the result by a count taken from the global, and stores it through the pointer argument. It also reads the vertical beam position register, and the purpose of the routine is not established by the pseudo-code.

name: setup_copper_list_and_sprites
description: Waits until a flag is set, clears several global values, and writes the copper list pointer, display control, interrupt and DMA registers, and the sprite registers. It calls eight other routines.

name: start_blit_after_wait
description: Waits for the blitter to become idle, then writes its modulo, destination pointer, control and size values, which starts a blit.

name: compute_scaled_division_table
description: Fills an eight-entry table, each entry being a global value shifted left by 10 bits and divided by a stored divisor. Each element uses a signed 16-bit division.

name: start_blit_with_control_word
description: Waits for the blitter to become idle, then writes a control word built from a shifted value combined with a fixed low part of 3066.

name: setup_full_blit_operation
description: Waits for the blitter, then configures its masks, modulos, source and destination pointers, control words and size for a blit, and calls two other routines.

name: scan_table_after_raster_wait
description: Waits until a global value reaches a fixed level, then walks a table of 16-bit entries while reading the beam position register.

name: scan_table_after_raster_wait
description: Variant of the raster-wait table scan that starts from a different initial count, reading the beam position register in the same way.

name: compute_packed_position_word
description: Computes a scaled value from a global offset by subtracting 5000 and dividing by 200 against a base of 3200, then packs two derived fields into a word stored in a global.

name: accumulate_with_carry_copy
description: Stores a pointer argument, copies a longword between two pointers, and accumulates a value with carry from a global over a loop count of 103. It calls one other routine.

name: run_blit_accumulation_loop
description: Waits for the blitter, configures its full register set, and runs a 128-step loop that adds values with carry. The pseudo-code does not fully establish the row pattern of the output.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Decodes as bad instruction data, so the pseudo-code stops at once and the bytes do not form a usable routine.

name: return_without_action
description: A single-instruction routine in another code segment with no visible work, so it returns immediately.

name: install_jump_patches_and_chain
description: Calls a routine through a pointer in its argument, links the argument into a structure field, and writes jump instructions into code locations to install hooks. It calls four other routines and a one-instruction routine.

name: patch_code_nops_and_jumps
description: Writes no-operation words and jump instructions over several code locations, and clears a block of 2000 words. It calls three other routines.

name: clear_block_and_call
description: Clears a block of 31 entries, sets two global values, and calls one other routine.

name: patch_code_with_jump_hooks
description: Writes jump instructions and no-operation pairs into several code locations and sets a mode flag to 2. It calls three other routines and a one-instruction routine.

name: read_cia_serial_key_byte
description: Reads the serial data register of the first CIA, clears it, rotates the byte into inverted form, and sets bits in a global status word before calling one other routine. The facts also list the interrupt request and beam position registers as touched.

name: store_byte_branch_on_four
description: Stores the low byte of its first argument into a global location, and branches to another target when the second argument and a global both equal 4. Otherwise it writes the byte to several more globals.

name: store_byte_branch_on_four
description: Works like its neighbour: it stores a byte into globals and branches when a pair of arguments both equal 4.

name: store_byte_to_globals
description: Stores a single byte argument into three global locations and calls two other routines.

name: store_byte_to_globals
description: Stores a single byte argument into three global locations and calls two other routines.

name: store_byte_to_global
description: Stores a byte argument into a single global location and calls one other routine.

name: store_byte_to_global
description: Stores a byte value into a global location. It is called from several places and does nothing else visible.

name: walk_buffer_with_calls
description: Computes pointer ranges from its counts and walks a buffer while calling five other routines.

name: return_without_action
description: Contains five instructions and performs no observable work, so it returns immediately.

name: select_global_table_byte
description: Selects a byte entry from a global table at a fixed index and calls two other routines.

name: repeat_calls_by_count
description: Obtains a count from another routine and calls routines in a loop until the count reaches minus one, then makes one final call.

name: wait_until_zero_results
description: Calls another routine repeatedly until it returns zero, then repeats a second wait-for-zero loop and makes a final call.

name: read_four_bytes_into_longword
description: Builds a 32-bit value by shifting in four successive bytes read through a pointer, advancing the pointer each time. The result is returned in the data register.

name: locate_packed_block_entry
description: Reads a size byte and offset fields from a packed block to compute the addresses of an entry and its last byte, then calls one other routine.

name: decode_bytes_backwards
description: Walks bytes backwards from a pointer, combining each with a running value and storing the decoded byte back in place. It calls two other routines.

name: decode_bytes_backwards
description: Continues the backward byte decoding with a counter-controlled loop. It calls one other routine.

name: call_table_entry_84
description: Calls a routine through a table entry 84 bytes into a stored base structure, then returns.

name: forward_two_calls
description: Calls two other routines in sequence and returns. It adds no other work.

name: call_single_unnamed_routine
description: Makes one call to another routine and returns.

name: call_table_entry_40
description: Calls a routine through a table entry 40 bytes into a stored base structure. It is referenced from two places.

name: return_without_action
description: Makes no meaningful changes and returns; the only work is a constant store that has no visible effect.

name: setup_display_registers_and_copy
description: Copies a block of words into a destination buffer, then sets the display window, data fetch, bitplane modulo and colour registers, the copper list pointer, and interrupt and DMA control values. It calls one other routine.

name: copy_words_into_three_planes
description: Copies words from a source into three bitplane areas that sit at fixed distances from the destination, stepping through fifteen entries.

name: clear_buffer_and_start_copper
description: Clears a block of 2000 words, then calls other routines, including one that points the copper at a new copper list. It calls five routines in total.

name: setup_display_window_registers
description: Writes display window, data fetch, bitplane modulo and control values to the display registers, and sets a fixed value into a global location.

name: enable_dma_channels
description: Writes a fixed value with bit 15 set to the DMA control register, which enables the DMA channels it selects.

name: set_interrupt_enable_mask
description: Writes an interrupt enable value with the top bit set, stores a routine address, then writes the mask 32767 to disable all interrupts. It calls one other routine.

name: count_entries_and_call
description: Writes 32 to a global location, calls another routine, and increments an entry counter. It is called from three places.

name: count_entries_and_call
description: Writes 32 to a global location and touches the interrupt request register, calls two other routines, and increments an entry counter.

name: adjust_byte_and_count
description: Adjusts a byte value by minus four, increments a counter, and stores a stack argument into a global location. It calls one other routine.

name: run_initialisation_sequence
description: Reads the first CIA port and writes the DMA control register, then calls ten other routines in sequence. The pseudo-code shows no further detail.

name: clear_block_and_call
description: Clears a block of 31 entries after adjusting a global value, and calls two other routines.

name: patch_byte_table_entries
description: Adjusts a byte in memory and clears bits in a table entry chosen by an index, then sets up a counter of 8000 for a later loop.

name: clear_large_memory_region
description: Clears a region of 8001 words starting at a pointer, then touches the background colour register and calls two other routines.

name: copy_words_into_three_planes
description: Copies four words from a source into a destination with bitplane-style offsets, writing to three areas spaced 20, 40 and 60 words apart.

name: poll_status_bit_loop
description: Reads a global count, calls several other routines, and loops while a status bit in a global stays set. It touches the first CIA port.

name: patch_byte_table_entries
description: Adjusts a byte in memory and clears bits in a table entry chosen by a masked index, in the same way as its neighbour, then continues with further byte updates.
